Once a query arrives, Hierarchical Latent Memory Evolution equips groups of latent memory tokens with progressively expanding memory receptive fields, enabling them to iteratively retrieve historical evidence from their corresponding scopes and internalize it into a compact, fixed-length latent memory. Finally, Progressive Confidence-guided Latent Memory Optimization constructs a hierarchical progression reward from group-wise predictive entropy and jointly refines the latent memory tokens and retrieved evidence, encouraging increasingly confident streaming reasoning. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LatentStream achieves new state-of-the-art results on existing online and offline video benchmarks.

AI.tldr: LatentStream introduces a progressive latent working memory for streaming video understanding, internalizing historical evidence into a compact latent memory to guide reasoning, outperforming prior store-and-retrieve methods.
AI.motivation: External external memory in streaming MLLMs stores history; this hinders internalization and efficient, causally bounded streaming reasoning. A compact, evolving latent memory can continuously guide reasoning without repeatedly retrieving raw history.
AI.method: 1) Query-agnostic Hierarchical Streaming Memory: organizes history into short-, mid-, long-term levels under a fixed budget via Jenks-guided adaptive consolidation. 2) Hierarchical Latent Memory Evolution: on query arrival, expands memory receptive fields; iteratively retrieves historical evidence from corresponding scopes and internalizes it into a fixed-length latent memory. 3) Progressive Confidence-guided Latent Memory Optimization: builds a hierarchical progression reward from group-wise predictive entropy and jointly refines latent memory tokens and retrieved evidence.
AI.result: Extensive experiments show state-of-the-art performance on existing online and offline video benchmarks, indicating effective streaming reasoning under memory constraints.
AI.conclusion: LatentStream demonstrates that shifting from store-and-retrieve external memory to retrieve-and-internalize latent memory yields superior streaming video understanding, with potential applicability to other streaming multimodal reasoning tasks.

title: Persistent Identity Preservation in Generative Image Models: A Benchmark and Evaluation System
summary: Generative image models can now produce high-quality images, follow complex instructions, and support precise edits, but they still struggle to preserve who or what is being depicted. When generating or editing images of a specific subject, identity may drift as the pose, expression, appearance, viewpoint, or surrounding scene changes. Existing subject-driven methods make fundamentally different choices about where identity is represented: through the input context (GPT-Image-2, NB2), as trainable subject-specific model parameters (LoRA), or as a persistent identity layer (PHOTA IDENTITY) reusable across generations and edits. We systematically benchmark these paradigms across subject-driven generation, editing, restoration, and multi-subject settings, with tasks designed to increasingly stress identity preservation. Our results show that identity preservation remains a distinct limitation of current generative foundation models: strong image quality and instruction following do not necessarily imply strong identity fidelity, and identity degradation becomes more pronounced under iterative edits, small subject scales, severe image degradation, and multi-subject composition. Persistent identity substantially reduces this degradation across generation, editing, and restoration, consistently improving identity preservation when applied to different foundation models while maintaining comparable instruction adherence and perceptual image quality. These results suggest that identity does not simply emerge from increasingly capable generative models, but can instead be represented as persistent subject knowledge that is composed independently with the underlying generative model.

AI.tldr: Persistent identity representations (PHOTA IDENTITY) outperform input-context and trainable-parameter approaches, mitigating identity drift across generation, editing, restoration, and multi-subject tasks; identity is best treated as persistent subject knowledge to be composed with the model.
AI.motivation: Identity preservation is a persistent limitation in generative models: quality and instruction-following do not guarantee faithful depiction of a subject; diverse paradigms encode identity differently (input context, LoRA, persistent identity) and require systematic benchmarking.
AI.method: Systematic benchmark across subject-driven generation, editing, restoration, and multi-subject settings; compare three paradigms (context-based, trainable parameters, persistent identity layer) under increasingly stressed conditions; evaluate identity fidelity and perceptual quality across models and edits.
AI.result: Identity fidelity is degraded by edits, small subject scale, degraded inputs, and multi-subject scenes; persistent identity significantly reduces degradation across tasks and models, with improved identity preservation while maintaining instruction adherence and perceptual quality.
AI.conclusion: Identity is not solely an emergent property of model capacity; representing identity as persistent subject knowledge that can be composed with generative models yields robust identity preservation across generation, editing, and restoration, suggesting a modular approach to identity in foundation models.

title: Zero-Shot Novel Depth Synthesis Using 3D Foundation Models Scene Representations
comment: Accepted to the European Conference on Computer Vision (ECCV) 2026. Project page: https://akola-mbey-denis.github.io/Z3D-page/
summary: 3D Foundation Models (3DFMs) such as VGGT have recently pushed the boundaries of 3D vision by predicting rich unified representations with feed-foward transformers. The scene representations learned by these models enable strong performance on multiple 3D vision tasks. In this paper, we investigate using their internal representations to infer 3D in the scene from new views. Our hypothesis is that in order to solve the task of 3D reconstruction, these models need to learn a representation that includes a large amount of general knowledge about 3D scenes. After showing that it is possible to decode hidden surfaces from internal 3DFM representations, we propose a method, Z3D, that estimates pointmaps in unseen views by doing latent diffusion on 3DFM representation. We show that Z3D can predict realistic depth maps for new views across multiple datasets.

AI.tldr: 3D foundation models' internal representations can be decoded to infer 3D structure from unseen views; introduces Z3D that uses latent diffusion on 3DFM representations to predict depth maps, achieving realistic results across datasets.
AI.motivation: Understand whether rich internal representations learned by 3D foundation models contain transferable 3D knowledge that can be exploited for novel-view depth estimation and reconstruction without training task-specific models.
AI.method: Demonstrate decoding of hidden surfaces from 3DFM representations; propose Z3D that performs latent diffusion in the 3DFM latent space to estimate pointmaps for unseen views, producing depth maps.
AI.result: Z3D yields realistic depth maps for new views across multiple datasets, indicating successful extraction of 3D information from internal 3DFM representations.
AI.conclusion: Internal 3DFM representations encode broad 3D scene knowledge; diffusion in their latent space is a viable approach for unseen-view depth estimation and 3D reconstruction; opens path to leveraging foundation models for 3D tasks.

title: Seeing Before Synthesizing: VLM-Guided Transition Event Discovery for Weakly-Supervised Dense Video Captioning
summary: Weakly-Supervised Dense Video Captioning aims to localize and describe multiple events in untrimmed videos given only an ordered set of event-level captions per video. Recent work synthesizes auxiliary transition captions via LLM to provide additional vision-language alignment, but these captions lack visual grounding and are rigidly assigned to every inter-event gap at a fixed location and duration. To address these, we propose Seeing Before Synthesizing (SBS), a framework that adaptively provides visually grounded linguistic guidance only where warranted. Leveraging a VLM, we generate frame-level narratives for the inter-event gaps and detect transitions from the semantic variation across them. For identified transitions, we then refine inter-event temporal masks by blending the temporal midpoint with the semantic change point and selecting the width that maximizes vision-language alignment. Experiments on ActivityNet Captions and YouCook2 demonstrate state-of-the-art performance in both captioning and localization.

AI.tldr: SBS adaptively grounds inter-event captions in weakly-supervised dense video captioning by using a vision-language model to generate frame-level narratives for event gaps, detect transitions, and refine temporal masks to maximize alignment, achieving state-of-the-art on ActivityNet Captions and YouCook2.
AI.motivation: Weakly-supervised dense video captioning relies on an ordered set of event-level captions but suffers from lack of visual grounding and rigid assignment of auxiliary transition captions to fixed inter-event gaps. A method that provides visually grounded guidance only where warranted could improve both caption quality and localization.
AI.method: Employ a pretrained vision-language model (VLM) to generate frame-level narratives for inter-event gaps. Detect transitions via semantic variation across these narratives. For identified transitions, refine inter-event temporal masks by blending the temporal midpoint with the semantic change point and selecting the width that maximizes vision-language alignment.
AI.result: Empirical evaluation on ActivityNet Captions and YouCook2 reports state-of-the-art performance in both dense-captioning quality and temporal localization.
AI.conclusion: The SBS framework delivers adaptive, visually grounded guidance for weakly-supervised dense video captioning, improving both captioning quality and localization by grounding inter-event gaps only when semantic transitions warrant it.

title: One Editor, Many Edits: A Unified Training-Free Framework for Diverse Video Editing
summary: Video editing spans diverse editing paradigms, yet achieving high-quality instruction-guided and subject-guided editing within a single unified framework remains challenging. We introduce EditVid, a training-free framework combining sparse causal memory for local coherence, correspondence-based post-attention token injection for long-range identity preservation, and soft latent blending for edit locality. The same framework supports instruction-guided and reference-guided edits, including style transfer, attribute modification, object insertion, part-level editing, and subject replacement. On FiVE, EditVid achieves 78.16 FiVE-Acc, compared with 58.95 for the strongest evaluated training-free baseline, while obtaining competitive results on IVEBench. A user study further shows a 51.8\% overall preference for EditVid over 7 competing methods.

AI.tldr: EditVid is a training-free, unified video-editing framework enabling instruction-guided and reference-guided edits within a single system, using sparse causal memory, token-injection attention, and soft latent blending to maintain local coherence and identity across edits.
AI.motivation: To address the challenge of achieving high-quality instruction-guided and subject-guided video editing within a single, training-free framework that preserves local coherence and identity over long sequences.
AI.method: Integrates three components: (1) sparse causal memory for local coherence; (2) correspondence-based post-attention token injection to preserve long-range identity; (3) soft latent blending to limit the scope of edits. The framework supports both instruction-guided and reference-guided edits (style transfer, attribute modification, object insertion, part-level editing, subject replacement) without additional training, and is evaluated on FiVE and IVEBench with user studies.
AI.result: On FiVE, EditVid achieves 78.16 FiVE-Acc, substantially higher than the strongest training-free baseline at 58.95, with competitive performance on IVEBench. A user study reports 51.8% overall preference over seven competing methods.
AI.conclusion: EditVid demonstrates a successful training-free, unified framework for diverse video edits, delivering strong quantitative gains and user preference, and enabling a broad range of edit types within a single system.

title: Puffin-World: Scaling a Unified Multimodal Model with Native 3D World States
summary: We propose Puffin-World, a unified multimodal architecture that integrates physical understanding, spatial simulation, and 3D world generation and reconstruction without relying on external offline modules. To reliably construct and interact with 3D worlds, our framework jointly models three native world states: physics (gravity field and latitude), geometry (depth), and appearance (image), together with a unified Omni-Camera representation that supports diverse tasks and flexible motions. Beyond modeling these states, we introduce a strategy for propagating physical dynamics across future frames. By grounding absolute camera properties in the real world, Puffin-World enables physically consistent and visually stable world generation. We further couple appearance and geometry within a single generative process, jointly synthesizing each future view and reconstructing its underlying geometry. This unified paradigm enables interleaved closed-loop applications requiring synergy across multiple tasks, including mimic and self-calibrated world exploration. To scale Puffin-World to complex scenarios, we construct Puffin-16M, comprising 15 million vision-language-camera triplets and 1 million trajectories featuring various and challenging motions. To foster further research in this area, we released the code, models, and datasets.

AI.tldr: Unified multimodal 3D world generation integrating physics, geometry, and appearance with an Omni-Camera; end-to-end trainable, closed-loop tasks; Puffin-16M dataset and release.
AI.motivation: Enable physically grounded, visually coherent 3D world generation without external offline modules by jointly modeling physics, geometry, and appearance and coupling them in a single generative process, scalable with a large multimodal dataset.
AI.method: Model native states—physics (gravity field and latitude), geometry (depth), and appearance (image)—jointly; use a unified Omni-Camera representation; propagate physical dynamics across future frames; ground absolute camera properties in the real world for consistency; couple appearance and geometry within a single generative process to synthesize future views and reconstruct geometry; enable interleaved closed-loop tasks (e.g., mimic, self-calibrated exploration); scale with Puffin-16M: 15M vision-language-camera triplets and 1M trajectories; release code, models, datasets.
AI.result: Claims physically consistent and visually stable 3D world generation; unified generation of future views with corresponding geometry; supports interleaved multi-task loops; scalable to complex scenarios; dataset and code released.
AI.conclusion: Proposes a unified, scalable framework for integrated perception, simulation, and rendering in 3D worlds, validated via a large-scale dataset release and multimodal architecture.

title: Principia: Relational Physics Tests for Video Models
summary: Evaluating physical reasoning in video models is difficult because absolute motion measurements depend on frame rate, object scale, and camera calibration, all of which are often ambiguous or unavailable in generated video. We propose a different approach. When two objects in the same scene obey the same physical law, their motions must satisfy predictable relationships, and these relationships hold independent of calibration. We introduce Principia, a benchmark that evaluates Newtonian physics through relational consistency between paired objects. Principia spans eight phenomena - gravity, restitution, friction, rotational inertia, projectile motion, momentum, pendulum, and mass-spring oscillation - across translational, rotational, collisional, and oscillatory dynamics, using real-world scenes recorded under controlled protocols. We also introduce a calibration-independent consistency score that quantifies physical violation directly in image space. Across thousands of generations from six state-of-the-art video generators, no model exceeds 0.42 on Principia despite all scoring around 0.8 on VBench. Vision-language models are evaluated on their ability to detect relational physics violations, with the best model achieving only 67% accuracy and most performing near chance level.

AI.tldr: Calibration-free relational physics benchmark (Principia) assesses Newtonian physics by relational consistency between paired objects across eight phenomena; models fail to capture physics, with low Principia scores compared to VBench; calibration-independent image-space score introduced.
AI.motivation: Absolute motion measurements depend on frame rate, scale, and calibration; need a relational, calibration-free evaluation of physical reasoning in video models.
AI.method: Create Principia spanning eight phenomena (gravity, restitution, friction, rotational inertia, projectile motion, momentum, pendulum, mass-spring) across translational, rotational, collisional, and oscillatory dynamics; use real-world scenes under controlled protocols; evaluate calibration-independent consistency between paired objects obeying same physical law; compute image-space consistency score; evaluate across video generators and vision-language models on relational violations.
AI.result: Models show weak performance: no generator exceeds 0.42 on Principia while VBench scores around 0.8; best vision-language model achieves 67% accuracy on detecting violations.
AI.conclusion: Principia provides a robust, calibration-independent benchmark for Newtonian physics and reveals a substantial gap in current video models' physical reasoning; encourages development of physics-aware models and improved evaluation methods.

title: Scal3R: Learning Efficient Multi-Relative Pose Query for Scalable Online 3D Reconstruction
summary: Online 3D reconstruction models perform poorly on long videos. This happens because regressing poses relative to a fixed first-frame anchor forces extrapolation far beyond the training distribution. Small drifts accumulate and amplify into significant geometric collapse. However, we observe that per-frame depth remains stable throughout this failure. The backbone's local geometry remains intact; only the global pose head breaks down. Motivated by this decoupling, we introduce Scal3R. This approach reformulates online reconstruction as multi-reference relative pose querying. We use lightweight learnable tokens, which make up about ~1% of the parameters, and inject them into a completely frozen backbone via asymmetric attention. This setup queries poses relative to multiple past keyframes. An online pose-graph optimization system with loop closure suppresses long-range drift. Scal3R reaches convergence in 8 hours on a single GPU. It reduces the average ATE by over 60% on KITTI compared to the online baseline. It also achieves state-of-the-art performance across Virtual KITTI, Sintel, TUM-Dynamic, ScanNet, and 7-Scenes. Project page: https://linjohnss.github.io/scal3r/

AI.tldr: Scal3R introduces multi-reference relative pose querying for online 3D reconstruction, decoupling pose regression from depth, and achieving strong gains with a frozen backbone and lightweight tokens; online pose-graph optimization with loop closure yields state-of-the-art results on several benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Online reconstruction on long videos suffers from drift when extrapolating relative to a fixed first-frame anchor; depth is stable but the global pose head breaks down, causing geometric collapse.
AI.method: Freeze the backbone and insert lightweight learnable tokens (~1% of parameters) via asymmetric attention to perform multi-reference relative pose querying against multiple past keyframes. Use online pose-graph optimization with loop closure to suppress long-range drift.
AI.result: Converges in 8 hours on a single GPU; reduces average ATE by over 60% on KITTI versus online baseline; achieves state-of-the-art results across Virtual KITTI, Sintel, TUM-Dynamic, ScanNet, and 7-Scenes.
AI.conclusion: Decoupling local geometry from global pose with multi-reference querying and loop-closure yields robust, scalable online reconstruction with strong empirical gains across diverse datasets.

title: TokenMatch: 3D Mesh Correspondence Transformer with Curvature-Guided Tokenisation
comment: 25 pages, 13 figures and 12 tables; project page: https://4dqv.mpi-inf.mpg.de/TokenMatch/
summary: While data-driven 3D shape correspondence estimation has recently seen substantial progress, robust matching under partial observations and strong non-isometric deformations remains challenging. Existing learning-based approaches often rely on hand-crafted descriptors or template-based representations, whereas recent generative models over functional maps suffer from high inference cost, limited interpretability, and poor generalisation to partial shapes. In response to these limitations, this paper introduces TokenMatch, a new transformer-based unified model for estimating 3D shape correspondences. Our feed-forward approach trained exclusively on BeCoS, a challenging non-isometric partial-to-partial shape-matching dataset, can generalise to matching full shapes without retraining or fine-tuning. TokenMatch uses self- and cross-attention mechanisms to efficiently learn patch-level and point-level relations as well as dense correspondences between shape pairs. Our core insight is that meshes can be adaptively tokenised into patches using shape curvature guidance, enabling effective learning of shape-specific geometric descriptors for correspondence estimation. We evaluate TokenMatch on standard benchmarks for partial and full shape matching, including CP2P, PSMAL, BeCoS, FAUST, SCAPE, and SHREC'19. Our method achieves consistently high performance, in most cases outperforming existing methods for partial and full shape matching in the mean geodesic error and intersection-over-union metrics, while also running faster at sub-second inference speeds.

AI.tldr: TokenMatch is a transformer-based model for 3D shape correspondence that tokenizes meshes into curvature-guided patches and learns dense patch- and point-level correspondences via self- and cross-attention, trained on BeCoS and generalizing to full shapes with sub-second inference.
AI.motivation: Robust 3D shape matching under partial observations and non-isometric deformations remains hard; existing methods rely on hand-crafted or template descriptors, while generative functional-map models suffer from high cost, poor interpretability, and poor partial-shape generalization.
AI.method: A unified transformer architecture using self- and cross-attention to learn patch-level and point-level relations and dense correspondences. Meshs are adaptively tokenised into patches guided by shape curvature to produce geometry-aware descriptors. Trained exclusively on BeCoS and evaluated on CP2P, PSMAL, BeCoS, FAUST, SCAPE, SHREC'19.
AI.result: TokenMatch achieves consistently high performance, often outperforming state-of-the-art methods for both partial and full shape matching in mean geodesic error and IoU metrics, while delivering sub-second inference speeds.
AI.conclusion: Curvature-guided tokenisation combined with transformer attention provides robust, efficient 3D shape correspondence; TokenMatch generalises to full shapes without retraining and improves partial-shape matching across standard benchmarks.

title: Temporal Self-Distillation: Learning Visual State Tracking in Videos Without Supervision
summary: We introduce S$^3$T (Self-Supervised Self-Distillation over Time), which, to the best of our knowledge, is the first fully self-contained framework for continuous video state tracking. Our method treats temporal sampling density as privileged information, based on the hypothesis that a denser view of the same clip recovers the running state more accurately. This view serves as the teacher, while a sparse-view student with the same weights learns to match its next-token distribution. The model generates its own target, so training requires no labels, separate teacher, or reward signal, and adds no inference cost. On LLaVA-OneVision-2-8B, S$^3$T improves VSTAT accuracy by $+1.74$ as a single model, $+2.38$ with souping, and $+2.70$ with additional vision-encoder adaptation, while prior self-evolving methods leave state tracking largely unchanged. The capability learned from unlabeled synthetic clips transfers to real videos, improving performance by $+7.95$ on VSTAT-YouTube state-tracking questions and $+4.50$ on MVBench Action Count.

AI.tldr: S^3T introduces a fully self-contained self-distillation framework for continuous video state tracking that uses dense temporal views as a teacher to train a sparse-view student with the same weights, requiring no labels or external teacher and adding no inference cost.
AI.motivation: To enable accurate continuous video state tracking without labeled data or external supervision by exploiting privileged dense temporal sampling as target guidance for a self-supervised, distillation-based approach.
AI.method: Dense-temporal views form the teacher signal; a sparse-view student with identical weights learns to match its next-token distribution. The model generates its own targets, eliminating the need for labels or separate teacher/reward signals and incurring no extra inference cost.
AI.result: On LLaVA-OneVision-2-8B: VSTAT accuracy improves by +1.74 (single model), +2.38 with souping, +2.70 with vision-encoder adaptation; prior self-evolving methods show little gain. Transfer to real videos yields +7.95 on VSTAT-YouTube state-tracking questions and +4.50 on MVBench Action Count.
AI.conclusion: S^3T delivers a fully self-contained, label-free approach that leverages temporal-density privileged information for continual video state tracking, yielding consistent gains on synthetic benchmarks and favorable transfer to real-video tasks, with no additional inference cost.
